correctness.rationale: The parity-set identity \(P_B\triangle\{\varphi(b_i)\}\) is an exact translation of the neighborhood condition at \(a_i\), and symmetrically for the other part. It proves that every proper coloring is odd for even \(n\), and that odd \(n\) requires at least three odd-sized color classes in each part. Properness confines every color shared by the two parts to one deleted matched pair, which forces the three-color boundary and the complete four-color structure. Independent enumeration over \(3\le n\le9\) checks every proper coloring through the claimed minimum palette and matches all counts.

value.rationale: Crown graphs are a classical dense bipartite family. The theorem reveals a sharp parity transition from \(2\) to \(4\), isolates the unique \(n=3\) boundary, and classifies and counts every optimum. The result also gives an infinite natural separation from proper conflict-free coloring, whose requirement is stronger and remains at four colors on even crowns.
